issues.description: The problem statement and the template declare and describe PersonService.addParent with the parameter order (Person person, Person parent). In the solution implementation the method declaration uses the parameters in reversed order (Person parent, Person person). Although both parameters have the same type so the code still compiles and PersonResource calls the method with (person, parent), the reversed parameter order in the solution is a structural inconsistency that can confuse students when comparing signatures and reading the implementation against the specification.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the parameter order and names consistent across artifacts. Change the solution method signature to match the problem and template: public Person addParent(Person person, Person parent) { ... } (and adjust the implementation variable names accordingly), or alternatively update the problem statement and template to intentionally use the reversed parameter order — prefer keeping (person, parent) to match the documented behavior.

issues.description: The problem statement and the template define PersonService.addParent with the signature addParent(Person person, Person parent) (person first, parent second). In the solution, the implemented method uses parameter names and ordering addParent(Person parent, Person person), i.e. the parameters are swapped. This discrepancy in parameter naming/order for the same conceptual operation (adding a parent to a person) creates cognitive mapping friction: the problem description, PersonResource usage (which calls addParent(person, parent)), and the template all expect the (person, parent) ordering, whereas the solution's parameter names suggest the opposite ordering.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename and reorder the solution method parameters to match the problem and template: change the solution signature to public Person addParent(Person person, Person parent) and update the implementation to treat the first parameter as the child (person) and the second as the parent. This keeps PersonResource calls and the problem description aligned and reduces student confusion.
